note: Rebuilt on every run of .github/workflows/daily-creator-pull.yml from the hooks harvested that day. Spyglass HOOK/USP aggregation returns empty for these creators because it is tuned to paid campaigns, so the patterns are read off the organic hooks themselves. Every quote is verified against a harvested hook before it is written.

patterns.label: cuts in on a question to an expert
patterns.description: Starts with the interviewer's question rather than any intro, dropping the viewer into a conversation already underway. It works because you appear to be overhearing something private rather than being addressed.

examples.creator: Michael Llanas
examples.quote: I really want to deep dive into owner financing because I know that's what you specialize in

examples.creator: 𝘾𝘼𝙈𝙀𝙍𝙊𝙉 𝙊𝙇𝙄𝙑𝙀𝙍𝘼  📍ℂ𝕙𝕚𝕔𝕒𝕘𝕠
examples.quote: I guess what areas do you invest in, how frequently?

examples.creator: Sean Pan
examples.quote: Does it matter if you intend to have like housemates and stuff like that?

examples.creator: Ravi Sharma
examples.quote: So how do you adapt post budget around building wealth with property?

examples.creator: Jerry Norton
examples.quote: What would a package deal look like if I bought this and Iowa?

patterns.label: states the belief then undercuts it
patterns.description: Voices what everyone in the audience thinks or fears — a common term, a common fear, a common conclusion — with framing that signals it is about to be dismantled. The viewer stays to find out whether they are the one who is wrong.

examples.creator: Sean Pan
examples.quote: Real estate investors love throwing around terms like cash on cash return.

examples.creator: Michael Llanas
examples.quote: Most up to investors when they're looking at their first up to deal, everyone's always scared of the due on sale clause.

examples.creator: Scott Betley
examples.quote: I got a buyer right now with a 3 % down payment and they want to wait a year because they think buying a home right now is stupid.

patterns.label: leads with a hard number result
patterns.description: Front-loads a precise figure or a ranking claim already achieved, so credibility arrives before the teaching does. The specificity of the number is what makes it feel like a receipt rather than a boast.

examples.creator: Sean Pan
examples.quote: I bought this 4plex for $250,000 and this is how much I make from it.

examples.creator: Jack Henderson
examples.quote: We just finished building it, and we made a sneaky, "one and a half million bucks" along the way.

examples.creator: Jeremy Werden
examples.quote: Five years ago, we turned this into North Carolina's number one Airbnb.

patterns.label: asks the question you would search
patterns.description: Opens with the exact query the target viewer would type, sometimes with a year attached, so the video announces itself as the answer to a question already in their head. No context is needed for the line to land.

examples.creator: Avery Carl
examples.quote: How much will an Airbnb make in 2026?

examples.creator: Logan Fullmer
examples.quote: How to find houses for cheap.

examples.creator: Jack Henderson
examples.quote: How to become a young... investor.

patterns.label: names a rule nobody knows yet
patterns.description: Opens by naming a specific piece of legislation or a new regulation by name, betting the viewer has never heard of it. The unfamiliar proper noun creates an information gap that feels urgent because it is official and already in motion.

examples.creator: Scott Betley
examples.quote: Hey Kyle, have you heard about the MOVE Act that Congress just proposed that can help homeowners keep their lower interest rates?

examples.creator: Scott Kuru
examples.quote: If the government's new SMSF property rules have got you thinking, "Fine, I can't borrow for residential anymore. I'll just buy commercial."

patterns.label: gives the answer in line one
patterns.description: Delivers the actionable payoff immediately, with no setup, so the rest of the video becomes the explanation rather than the reveal. It earns attention by proving the video has a real answer instead of teasing one.

examples.creator: Theoni Rapo
examples.quote: If the house that you like on Zillow is still on the market, ask for a seller credit.

examples.creator: Logan Fullmer
examples.quote: One of the best places in all the land to buy distressed property is right here, your county courthouse.

patterns.label: opens inside a real phone call
patterns.description: The first words are actual deal dialogue — an introduction to a seller, a comment on comps — so the viewer arrives mid-transaction. Unscripted stakes are the draw; something real is happening and could go either way.

examples.creator: Jerry Norton
examples.quote: Hi Peter, my name is Jerry Norton calling you about your property on Liberty Road.

examples.creator: 𝘾𝘼𝙈𝙀𝙍𝙊𝙉 𝙊𝙇𝙄𝙑𝙀𝙍𝘼  📍ℂ𝕙𝕚𝕔𝕒𝕘𝕠
examples.quote: Yeah, I checked the comps on this one.

patterns.label: reports a deal happening right now
patterns.description: Frames the video as a live dispatch from an in-progress deal — an offer just made, an approval just granted. The present tense makes it news rather than a lesson, so watching feels time-sensitive.

examples.creator: Jerry Norton
examples.quote: So Jared and I are out here at a house in Maryville that Jared made an offer on.

examples.creator: Jack Henderson
examples.quote: Another council approval has just come through for one of our Henderson equity factory deals.

patterns.label: points at something on screen
patterns.description: Uses a demonstrative — this house, your house — that only makes sense if you look, forcing the eye to the frame before the brain decides to scroll. The line is meaningless without the visual, which is exactly what holds you.

examples.creator: Jack Henderson
examples.quote: You see this little house here?

examples.creator: Erick Brice
examples.quote: This is your house This is your house Hey

patterns.label: promises a reveal with no content
patterns.description: Says nothing at all except that something is coming, relying entirely on tone and an open loop. It works only with an audience that already trusts the creator to make the payoff worth it.

examples.creator: Scott Betley
examples.quote: Y'all guess what happened?

examples.creator: Michael Llanas
examples.quote: So check this out

patterns.label: names a money target and a deadline
patterns.description: Pairs a specific dollar amount with a short, near-term window — two weeks, tonight — turning the video into a countdown the viewer wants to see resolved. The tight timeframe is what makes the number feel testable rather than hypothetical.

examples.creator: 𝘾𝘼𝙈𝙀𝙍𝙊𝙉 𝙊𝙇𝙄𝙑𝙀𝙍𝘼  📍ℂ𝕙𝕚𝕔𝕒𝕘𝕠
examples.quote: Let's have AI make us 10 grand in two weeks.

examples.creator: Emeline SIRON - Experte investissement immobilier
examples.quote: Cette nuit, tu vas gagner de l'argent en dormant.

patterns.label: opens on the crowd panicking
patterns.description: Leads with the emotional temperature of the market — everyone is scared, everything is falling, is it dead — rather than with data. The viewer stays because they were already feeling it and want to be told what it means. (single example)

examples.creator: Ravi Sharma
examples.quote: Prices are falling and people are freaking out

patterns.label: tells you not to do something
patterns.description: Opens as a prohibition against a purchase or feature the viewer probably wants, then withholds the reason. The negative command interrupts an existing plan, which is harder to scroll past than an invitation. (single example)

examples.creator: Jeremy Werden
examples.quote: Do not buy a lakefront or beachfront property unless you consider this.
